la:verb:comburo.gloss: to burn up, to burn away
senses: to burn up, to burn away
la:verb:comburo.html:
com-būro (conb-), ussi, ustum, ĕre, v. a.
root bur-, pur-; cf. burrus, Gr. πυρρός, pruna, Gr. πίμπρημι, and Lat. bustum
,
to burn up, consume (class.).
Prop.: quae potuere Nec cum capta capi, nec cum combusta cremari, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 360 Vahl.): fumo comburi nihil potest,: flamma comburens impete magno,: is ejus (solis) tactus est, ut saepe comburat,: aedis,: frumentum omne,: naves,: annales,; cf. ; Liv 33, 11, 1: religiosas vestes, * : aliquem vivum,; Auct. B. Hisp. 20; so of persons: et patrem et filium vivos conburere,; Serv ap. ; .—Hence,
P. a., as subst.' combu-stum, i, n., a burn, a wound made by burning combusta sanare, : combustis mederi,. —
Trop. comburere aliquem judicio, to ruin, destroy, (v. the passage in connection). So to be consumed by love, * . diem to pass it in carousing, q. s. to bear it to its grave (the figure borrowed from burning dead bodies), .
